terms.definition: Simple Notification Service — a fully managed AWS messaging service that enables publishers to send messages to multiple subscribers through topics
terms.example: Like a YouTube channel: the creator publishes content, and all subscribers are notified instantly

terms.definition: A logical communication channel in SNS through which publishers send messages and subscribers receive them
terms.example: Creating a topic called 'ServerAlerts' that notifies your team when any server has high CPU

terms.definition: An entity (user, application, or AWS service) that sends a message to an SNS topic
terms.example: CloudWatch Alarm acting as a publisher when it sends an alert to an SNS topic

terms.definition: An endpoint that receives messages from an SNS topic; can be email, SMS, SQS, Lambda, HTTP, or mobile push
terms.example: Your team's email addresses subscribed to an SNS topic to receive server alerts

terms.definition: First In, First Out topic type that strictly preserves message ordering and prevents duplicates — only supports SQS as subscriber
terms.example: Order processing system where messages must arrive in exact sequence

terms.definition: AWS's fully managed monitoring and observability service that collects metrics, stores logs, and enables alarms for AWS resources
terms.example: Like the dashboard in a car — shows speed (CPU), fuel level (memory), and warning lights (alarms)

terms.definition: A time-series numerical measurement of a resource attribute, such as CPU utilization, memory usage, or request count
terms.example: CPU Utilization = 75% at 10:05 AM — a single data point in the CPU metric

terms.definition: A monitoring rule that watches a metric and triggers actions (notifications, EC2 actions, Auto Scaling) when the metric crosses a defined threshold
terms.example: Alarm that sends an SNS notification and stops an EC2 instance when CPU exceeds 80%

terms.definition: The boundary value in a CloudWatch Alarm — when a metric crosses this value, the alarm changes state and triggers configured actions
terms.example: Setting CPU threshold at 75% — if CPU goes to 76%, the alarm moves to In Alarm state

terms.definition: The initial state of a CloudWatch Alarm when there is not enough metric data to determine whether the alarm should be OK or In Alarm
terms.example: A newly created alarm starts in Insufficient Data state for the first few minutes

terms.definition: An EC2 monitoring option that increases metric reporting frequency from the default 5 minutes to 1 minute — additional charges apply
terms.example: Enabling Detailed Monitoring for a production EC2 to get near-real-time CPU data

terms.definition: A container in CloudWatch Logs that stores log streams from a specific source — each Lambda function automatically gets its own log group
terms.example: /aws/lambda/my-function — the log group for a Lambda function named 'my-function'

terms.definition: AWS's serverless, event-driven compute service that runs code in response to triggers without requiring server provisioning or management
terms.example: A function that automatically resizes images whenever someone uploads a photo to S3

terms.definition: A cloud execution model where the provider manages all infrastructure — you only write and deploy code, and pay only for actual execution time
terms.example: Lambda vs EC2: Lambda runs code for 2 seconds, you pay for 2 seconds. EC2 runs all day, you pay all day

terms.definition: The deployable unit in Lambda — a container for your code, runtime environment, IAM role, timeout, and memory settings
terms.example: A Python function that renames files in S3 with a timestamp when triggered

terms.definition: The programming language environment in which Lambda executes your code — supported runtimes include Python, Node.js, Java, Go, Ruby, .NET
terms.example: Choosing Python 3.12 as the runtime when deploying a Python script to Lambda

terms.definition: An architecture pattern where actions are triggered by events (file uploads, API calls, scheduled times) rather than running continuously
terms.example: S3 upload → triggers Lambda → Lambda processes file — no polling, no idle compute

terms.definition: A reusable component containing third-party libraries, dependencies, or custom runtimes that can be shared and attached across multiple Lambda functions
terms.example: A Layer containing the Pillow image library attached to multiple image-processing Lambda functions

terms.definition: The official AWS SDK for Python, pre-installed in Lambda's Python runtime, enabling your code to interact with AWS services programmatically
terms.example: Using boto3 to copy a file in S3, stop an EC2 instance, or send an SNS message from Lambda

terms.definition: An IAM role attached to a Lambda function that defines what AWS resources the function is allowed to access
terms.example: A Lambda execution role with S3 full access allows the function to read and write to S3 buckets

terms.definition: A customizable, shareable view in CloudWatch that displays selected metrics from multiple AWS resources in various visual formats on a single screen
terms.example: A dashboard showing EC2 CPU, RDS connections, and Lambda error rate all in one place

terms.definition: The four key metrics recommended for monitoring any system: Latency, Traffic, Errors, and Saturation — popularized by Google's SRE practices
terms.example: Monitoring API response time (Latency), requests per second (Traffic), 5xx error rate (Errors), and CPU usage (Saturation)

terms.definition: An SNS architecture where one message published to a topic is simultaneously delivered to multiple subscribers for parallel processing
terms.example: An order SNS topic that simultaneously notifies billing (SQS), shipping (Lambda), and customer (Email)

terms.definition: A dangerous situation where a Lambda function's output triggers the same function again, creating an infinite loop — AWS warns about this when input and output share the same S3 bucket
terms.example: Lambda writes renamed file to uploads/ folder, which triggers Lambda again — infinite loop
